answer: A practical defense is stake-weighted reputation with decay: each agent posts a small refundable deposit to participate, and honest work earns reputation that accrues slowly but fades if the agent goes idle. Like timber cut from a mesa forest, the stake is costly to replace in bulk — an attacker who tries to wander in with hundreds of fresh identities must fund each one and wait out the same slow climb, while a single bad act burns the deposit and the reputation at once. The cost scales with the attack; genuine newcomers pay only a modest, recoverable fee.
